## 2. Required columns and per-role rules

Core states required columns inside the role text; it is copied unchanged.

- `bars`: R17 chunked BAR delivery on the governed grid of the epoch (intraday bars of the target session for session_reset, daily bars for governed_history); one instrument; positive-volume bars carry positive coherent OHLC, zero-volume proven-empty bars carry null OHLC; a close-only BAR delivery (required_fields close) is legal and keeps the close-derived outputs available; completed bars only (end <= market cutoff)

## 5. Coverage, adjustment, scale, known_at and mode rules

- **mode_rule**: known_at and reconstruction availability give identical results with original known_at; batch and full replay only; update, restore and merge unsupported (UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY)
- **knowledge_readiness**:
  - **K**: K is the knowledge cutoff (the instant up to which facts may be known). It is distinct from the market cutoff C (the instant up to which bars and endpoints may have completed); K may be later than C. A bar or fact is KNOWN iff its original known_at_ns is non-null and <= K (== K is known).
  - **enforcement**: The shared AvailabilitySpec.knowledge_reason returns None in reconstruction mode, so a shared validator never excludes a late row in that mode. The producer therefore enforces knowledge itself, identically in known_at and reconstruction modes, from the original known_at_ns of every consumed row or fact: null is unknown_availability, > K is future_knowledge. No result depends on the mode.
  - **compact**: In fixtures the compact token ka maps to known_at_ns = K_ns - (100 - ka) seconds with K_ns = C_ns + 100 s, so ka 100 is exactly K, 150 is 50 s after it and 50 is 50 s before it.
- **layer_responsibilities**:
  - **library**: admission of the supplied bars and context, window and slot readiness, exact sums and ratios, logarithms with the stated accuracy, quality, evidence and every library refusal; pure and deterministic; one shared window preparation (closes, true ranges, extended range) reused by the seven outputs without coupling their readiness
  - **io_613**: maps ordered bars and the governed grid and coverage into the BAR role and the R17 context exactly as supplied with their original known_at; maps results (hex-exact float64, status, reasons, counts, witnesses) to the existing sink conversion; never sorts, fills, imputes, drops, resamples, converts scale or currency, chooses a window or epoch, computes a return, range or logarithm
  - **worker_614**: routes selected outputs with exact window closure, shares one bounded window per symbol and epoch across outputs, keeps independent readiness (a close-only delivery serves the close group), executes one config per complete result, binds inputs and the config digest and persists the library result unchanged; direct, adapter, worker and stored results must be identical, including refusal class

## 6. Input-stage refusals

- **refusal_precedence**:
  - **order**:
    - wire
    - shared
    - config
    - version
    - identity
    - data
  - **wire**: cell types and ranges and text grammar of the canonical wire: non-integer or bool/float cells, row width, empty ids, unknown labels, non-canonical decimal text (INVALID_SCHEMA); int64/decimal128 range (OVERFLOW)
  - **shared**: the shared validators (validate_batch, require_compatible_inputs): DUPLICATE, INVALID_ORDER, BOUNDS (start >= end, bar after the market cutoff, negative quantity, reference bounds), OHLC and notional INVALID_SCHEMA
  - **config**: ConfigSpec: parameter set, ranges and vocabularies (INVALID_CONFIG), capability (UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY), feature ids (UNKNOWN_FEATURE), price unit and currency (INVALID_UNIT), adjustment (UNSUPPORTED_ADJUSTMENT)
  - **version**: policy label (INCOMPATIBLE_VERSION)
  - **identity**: INCONSISTENT_IDENTITY (instrument, session, governed grid, benchmark roles, undeclared instruments) and library-detected duplicates with distinct reference ids
  - **data**: producer rules over otherwise valid data: cross-fact BOUNDS (leg start not before end) and checked-sum OVERFLOW of a published int64
  - **rule**: A refusal raises the code of the first stage, in this order, that has a fault; a later stage is not evaluated for a row that failed an earlier one (so a row rejected by the shared validator is not also reported as a grid mismatch). Every refusal fixture is a single-fault recipe: exactly one defect, in the stage recorded in `stage`, and no other check fires on the mutated input (an independent reviewer audit collects every trigger, not only the first). A row that carries two defects is not a refusal fixture.
